title: Standardize 429 error payload copy + Console/docs snippets for enterprise priority & quotas
creator: Elliot Price
content:
## Context
Hot-route capacity protection introduces tier-aware rate limits/quotas, admission control, and controlled shedding. Customers will see more *intentional* 429s (best-effort earlier, enterprise protected) and Support needs deterministic, consistent language to explain what happened.

We currently have inconsistent copy across:
- API JSON error responses (varies by service)
- Streaming termination behavior (some clients see abrupt disconnects)
- Redwood Console internal operator surfaces (recent overload events)
- Developer docs snippets (retry guidance, reason codes)

This ticket defines the canonical copy blocks and wording constraints so that:
1) API responses are stable and parseable (code/reason), and the message is human-friendly.
2) Docs and Console use the same terms (quota vs rate limit vs overload shedding).
3) We avoid promising behavior we can’t guarantee (e.g., “your request will succeed if you retry”).

## Scope
### In
- Standardized human-readable error messages for 429 responses and streaming termination.
- Terminology and microcopy guidelines for Console / internal operator UI (not customer-visible Console UI yet, but copy should be future-proof).
- Docs snippets: recommended client retry/backoff text, plus how to interpret headers.

### Out
- Defining the full schema / headers (owned by ENG-4922 + ENG-4923). This ticket only provides copy + naming conventions to be used consistently.
- Pricing/billing language.

## Canonical terminology
Use these terms consistently in all surfaces:
- **Rate limit**: short window (seconds/minutes), request-based throttle (e.g., RPM). Typically recoverable quickly.
- **Quota**: longer window (hour/day/month), usage-based cap. Not recoverable until window resets or limit is increased.
- **Overload protection**: platform-driven admission control/shedding due to fleet pressure. May be short-lived; retry may succeed, but we must guide backoff.
- **Priority tier**: customer tier classification used for protection decisions. Avoid exposing internal tier labels (e.g., “priority class 0/1”) to customers.

Avoid:
- “Banned”, “blocked”, “blacklisted”, “punished”
- “Guaranteed” (e.g., “retry will succeed”)
- “Degraded tier” as a customer-facing phrase

## Error message patterns (customer-facing)
These are the canonical `error.message` strings. Keep them stable; only adjust punctuation if necessary.

### 1) Rate limit exceeded (short-window throttle)
**Message:** "Rate limit exceeded. Please retry after a short delay."
**When to use:** per-route/per-key short-window limits.
**Docs addendum snippet:** "Use exponential backoff with jitter. Respect `Retry-After` if present."

### 2) Quota exceeded (long-window cap)
**Message:** "Quota exceeded for this route. Please wait for your quota window to reset or contact support to increase limits."
**When to use:** daily/monthly token/request quotas.

### 3) Overload protection / admission control active
**Message:** "Request throttled due to temporary capacity protection. Please retry with backoff."
**When to use:** routing/runtime admission control due to fleet pressure (queue depth/scheduler lag) when the platform is protecting higher-SLA traffic.

### 4) Burst limit exceeded (explicit burst allowance)
**Message:** "Burst limit exceeded. Reduce request concurrency or retry with backoff."
**When to use:** burst-specific checks (if we expose this separately from rate limit).

### 5) Streaming termination due to capacity protection
If we must terminate an in-flight stream, the final observable error should match the overload message above.
**Message (same as #3):** "Request throttled due to temporary capacity protection. Please retry with backoff."
**Implementation note:** Ensure the surface (SSE/event stream vs HTTP body) includes the same `error.code`/`error.reason` fields as non-streaming 429s, when possible.

## Reason code naming guidance
Engineering owns the exact enumeration, but copy must map 1:1. Recommended customer-safe reason names (snake_case):
- `rate_limit_exceeded`
- `quota_exceeded`
- `capacity_protection`
- `burst_limit_exceeded`

If Engineering needs more detailed internal reasons (e.g., `scheduler_lag_high`, `queue_depth_high`, `best_effort_shed`), keep those internal-only or behind an admin/debug endpoint. Customer-facing reason codes should remain stable and not reveal fleet internals.

## Console / internal operator UI copy
These strings are intended for internal-only Console views and incident-bot style messages. Still keep them clear and non-blamey; they will be pasted into customer comms.

### Overload protection banner (internal)
"Capacity protection is active for one or more hot routes. Best-effort traffic may be throttled to preserve enterprise SLOs."

### Event row label
- Title: "Capacity protection activation"
- Subtitle: "Admission control engaged to preserve protected-route budgets"

### Tooltip text for shed rate
"Share of requests rejected with 429 due to capacity protection (not quota)."

## Developer docs snippets (copy-ready)
### Retry guidance (generic)
"If you receive a 429, you can retry the request. Use exponential backoff with jitter and cap max retries. If `Retry-After` is present, wait at least that long before retrying."

### Distinguish quota vs overload
"A 429 may indicate rate limiting/quota enforcement or temporary capacity protection. Check the error `reason` and response headers to determine whether to wait for a quota reset or to retry with backoff."

### Support escalation sentence (enterprise)
"If you are on an enterprise plan and observe sustained 429s with reason `capacity_protection` during normal traffic patterns, contact support with request IDs and timestamps so we can review your route budgets and exceptions."

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] PM + SRE agree on terminology and customer-safe phrasing.
- [x] Copy blocks above are posted in the PRD/design references (PM-883) and linked from ENG-4922/ENG-4930.
- [x] Docs PR uses these messages verbatim (or includes an explicit note if technical constraints require minor edits).
- [x] Streaming termination uses same canonical overload message.

## References / links
- Project overview: Hot-route capacity protection (ENG-4921)
- Gateway implementation: ENG-4922
- Support playbook: ENG-4930
- Draft customer messaging: PM-883
- Docs update PR: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-2217-document-429-reason-codes-and-retry-guidance.json

## Open questions
1) Do we expose tier language explicitly (e.g., “best-effort”)? Current recommendation: avoid mentioning tiers in customer-facing 429 messages; keep to “capacity protection.”
2) Do we want separate copy for Dedicated vs Hosted? Recommendation: same messages; docs can clarify plan-specific limits.
3) Do we include “contact support” in overload message? Recommendation: only in docs (not the base API message) to keep API responses concise and avoid implying overload is always support-worthy.
comments: 2025-12-11 — Nikhil Sharma (PM): Please avoid phrasing that implies we are "prioritizing other customers". "Capacity protection" framing is good; keep tier mentions out of the default message.
2025-12-13 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): +1 to keeping internal signal detail out of customer reason codes. We can include queue/scheduler specifics in the admin debug endpoint only.

2025-12-16 — Amara Diallo (Gateway): We can support stable `reason` values; message string should be stable as well. For streaming, we can ensure the terminal event includes the same fields, but exact mechanics depend on client protocol.
2026-01-07 — Dev Patel (Support): Please include a copy-ready escalation sentence for enterprise customers + guidance to share request IDs/timestamps. Added to docs snippet section.
2026-01-14 — Chloe Martin (Console): Internal operator banner/tooltips look good. We’ll reuse these strings in the initial internal-only Console hooks (ENG PR planned).
2026-01-22 — Wei Chen: Landed in docs PR (redwood-docs#2217) and cross-linked from ENG-4922. Marking Done.
